questions.knowledge_point: Identifying Partitions of the Real Line
questions.problem:
Which of the following are partitions of the real interval $[-3,7]?$

- ${-3,-5,1,2,6}$
- ${-3,0,3,7,8}$
- ${-3,-2,1,3,4,7}$
questions.worked_solution:
A partition $P$ of a closed interval $[a,b]$ is a finite sequence of real numbers taken from $[a,b]$ such that

$$
a={x}_{0}<{x}_{1}<{x}_{2}<…<{x}_{n}=b\,.
$$

We can express $P$ using set notation as

$$
P={{x}_{0},{x}_{1},…,{x}_{n}}.
$$

 

With that in mind, let's consider each statement:

- Statement I is not a partition of $[-3,7]$ since it does not include the right endpoint $b=7.$

- Statement II is not a partition of $[-3,7]$ since $8$ does not belong to $[-3,7].$

- Statement III is a partition of $[-3,7].$

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only."

choices.value: None of the statements give a partition of $[-3,7]$

questions.knowledge_point: Computing Simple Sums Over Partitions of the Real Line
questions.problem: Let $P={{z}_{0},{z}_{1},…,{z}_{q}}$ be a partition of the interval $[4,9].$ If $Δ{z}_{k}={z}_{k}-{z}_{k-1},$ calculate ${\sum }_{k=1}^{q}7Δ{z}_{k}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we take the factor $7$ outside the summation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{k=1}^{q}7Δ{z}_{k}=7{\sum }_{k=1}^{q}Δ{z}_{k}\end{aligned}
$$

Note that ${\sum }_{k=1}^{q}Δ{z}_{k}$ is just the length of the interval $[4,9],$ because

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{k=1}^{q}Δ{z}_{k} & =({z}_{1}-{z}_{0})+({z}_{2}-{z}_{1})+({z}_{3}-{z}_{2})+⋯+({z}_{q}-{z}_{q-1}) \\  & =(\cancel{{z}_{1}}-{z}_{0})+(\cancel{{z}_{2}}-\cancel{{z}_{1}})+(\cancel{{z}_{3}}-\cancel{{z}_{2}})+⋯+({z}_{q}-\cancel{{z}_{q-1}}) \\  & =-{z}_{0}+{z}_{q} \\  & ={z}_{q}-{z}_{0} \\  & =9-4 \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
7{\sum }_{k=1}^{q}Δ{z}_{k}=7\cdot 5=35.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Computing Simple Sums Over Partitions of the Real Line
questions.problem: Let $P={{x}_{0},{x}_{1},…,{x}_{m}}$ be a partition of the interval $[2,10].$ If $Δ{x}_{i}={x}_{i}-{x}_{i-1},$ calculate ${\sum }_{i=1}^{m}-4Δ{x}_{i}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we take the factor $(-4)$ outside the summation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}-4Δ{x}_{i}=-4{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}Δ{x}_{i}\end{aligned}
$$

Note that ${\sum }_{i=1}^{m}Δ{x}_{i}$ is just the length of the interval $[2,10],$ because

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}Δ{x}_{i} & =({x}_{1}-{x}_{0})+({x}_{2}-{x}_{1})+({x}_{3}-{x}_{2})+⋯+({x}_{m}-{x}_{m-1}) \\  & =(\cancel{{x}_{1}}-{x}_{0})+(\cancel{{x}_{2}}-\cancel{{x}_{1}})+(\cancel{{x}_{3}}-\cancel{{x}_{2}})+⋯+({x}_{m}-\cancel{{x}_{m-1}}) \\  & =-{x}_{0}+{x}_{m} \\  & ={x}_{m}-{x}_{0} \\  & =10-2 \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
-4{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}Δ{x}_{i}=(-4)\cdot 8=-32.
$$

questions.problem: Let $P={{x}_{0},{x}_{1},…,{x}_{m}}$ be a partition of the interval $[0,3].$ If $Δ{x}_{i}={x}_{i}-{x}_{i-1},$ calculate ${\sum }_{i=1}^{m}5Δ{x}_{i}.$
questions.worked_solution:
Using the constant multiple rule, we can write the summation as

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}5Δ{x}_{i}=5{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}Δ{x}_{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that ${\sum }_{i=1}^{m}Δ{x}_{i}$ is just the length of the interval $[0,3],$ because

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}Δ{x}_{i} & =({x}_{1}-{x}_{0})+({x}_{2}-{x}_{1})+({x}_{3}-{x}_{2})+⋯+({x}_{m}-{x}_{m-1}) \\  & =(\cancel{{x}_{1}}-{x}_{0})+(\cancel{{x}_{2}}-\cancel{{x}_{1}})+(\cancel{{x}_{3}}-\cancel{{x}_{2}})+⋯+({x}_{m}-\cancel{{x}_{m-1}}) \\  & =-{x}_{0}+{x}_{m} \\  & ={x}_{m}-{x}_{0} \\  & =3-0 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
5{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}Δ{x}_{i}=5\cdot 3=15.
$$

canonical_examples.problem:
Which of the following are partitions of the real interval $[1,9]?$

- $\{1, 4, 5, 8\}$

- $\{1, 3, 4, 9\}$

- $1 <     2  <    9$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
A partition $P$ of a closed interval $[a,b]$ is a finite sequence of real numbers taken from $[a,b]$ such that

$$
a = x_0 <      x_1<      x_2 <      \ldots <      x_n = b\,.
$$

We can express $P$ using set notation as

$$
P=\{x_0,x_1,\ldots,x_n\}.
$$

 

With that in mind, let's consider each statement:

- Statement I is not a partition of $[1,9]$ since it does not include the right endpoint $b=9.$

- Statement II is a partition of $[1,9].$

- Statement III is a partition of $[1,9].$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only."

canonical_examples.problem: Let $P= \left\{y_0, y_1, \ldots, y_n\right\}$ be a partition of the interval $[-3, 5].$ If $\Delta y_j = y_j - y_{j-1},$ calculate $\displaystyle \sum_{j=1}^n {3}\Delta y_j.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we take the factor $3$ outside the summation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}3Δ{y}_{j}=3{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}Δ{y}_{j}\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $\displaystyle \sum_{j=1}^n \Delta y_j$ is just the length of the interval $[-3, 5],$ because

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}Δ{y}_{j} & =Δ{y}_{1}+Δ{y}_{2}+Δ{y}_{3}+⋯+Δ{y}_{n} \\  & =({y}_{1}-{y}_{0})+({y}_{2}-{y}_{1})+({y}_{3}-{y}_{2})+⋯+({y}_{n}-{y}_{n-1}) \\  & =(\cancel{{y}_{1}}-{y}_{0})+(\cancel{{y}_{2}}-\cancel{{y}_{1}})+(\cancel{{y}_{3}}-\cancel{{y}_{2}})+⋯+({y}_{n}-\cancel{{y}_{n-1}}) \\  & =-{y}_{0}+{y}_{n} \\  & ={y}_{n}-{y}_{0} \\  & =5-(-3) \\  & =5+3 \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
{3}\sum_{j=1}^n \Delta y_j = 3 \cdot 8 = 24.
$$
